description: Comprehensive README documenting the PokeOps stack, offline constraints, install/build/seed/test/run instructions, the modular AI/pricing/marketplace interface boundaries, the database schema overview, and an explicit P0/P1/P2 feature status matrix (implemented vs stubbed). This is the final deliverable that lets a new developer run the app and understand what is real vs mocked.
steps: Reminder: zero deps, `unset NODE_OPTIONS`. This runs after FEAT-001..008 so the README reflects what actually exists. Read package.json scripts, tsconfig, the src/ directory layout, the interfaces in src/services/interfaces, and the seed script before writing.

Write /projects/sandbox/PSA/README.md covering: (1) Product summary (PokeOps - AI-powered Pokemon TCG Seller Operating System) and the core loop Scan -> Identify -> Value -> Single/Bulk -> Listing. (2) Tech stack and WHY: zero-dependency TypeScript on Node.js 22 built-ins (node:http, node:sqlite, node:crypto, node:test), compiled with the global TypeScript compiler; vanilla-TS/server-rendered frontend, hand-drawn SVG charts - chosen because the sandbox has NO npm registry access. (3) Requirements: Node.js 22+ (for node:sqlite). (4) The critical NODE_OPTIONS caveat: you must `unset NODE_OPTIONS` before build/test/run in this environment, and why. (5) Setup/run: `unset NODE_OPTIONS`, `npm run build`, `npm run seed`, `npm start`, open http://localhost:4000, demo login (demo@pokeops.local + password). (6) `npm test` to run the node:test suite. (7) Directory structure overview. (8) Database schema: list the 15 entities and their relationships. (9) Modular architecture / interface boundaries: document Recognizer, PricingEngine, ClassificationService, ListingGenerator, MarketplacePublisher, SellerAssistant - where each interface lives, that the current implementations are deterministic MOCKS, and exactly how a real CV model / real eBay-TCGplayer API / real price feed / real LLM drops in behind the same interface without touching the UI. (10) Feature status matrix: P0 (implemented), P1 (implemented where done), P2 (stubbed behind interfaces) with a short line per item from spec section 43. (11) Demo data note (section 44): data is seeded and flagged is_demo, clearly labeled in the UI. (12) Security notes (section 42): passwords hashed with scrypt, sessions, no marketplace credentials in the frontend. (13) Known limitations / future work: real integrations are out of scope offline; in-memory session store; experimental node:sqlite warning.
Ensure README commands exactly match the real package.json scripts and default port/paths. Include a short 'Offline / network-restricted build' note so the build strategy is reproducible.
acceptance_criteria: README.md exists at repo root and accurately documents the stack, the NODE_OPTIONS caveat, and the exact build/seed/test/run commands that work in this sandbox.

README documents all six modular interfaces (Recognizer, PricingEngine, ClassificationService, ListingGenerator, MarketplacePublisher, SellerAssistant), states they are currently mocked, and explains how real implementations plug in without UI changes.
README includes the 15-entity schema overview and a P0/P1/P2 feature status matrix (implemented vs stubbed).
Every command in the README, run from a clean checkout with NODE_OPTIONS unset, works (build, seed, test, start).
verification: unset NODE_OPTIONS; cd /projects/sandbox/PSA && npm run build && npm run seed && npm test  (confirm README commands succeed)
Manually re-read README.md and confirm the interface boundaries and P0/P1/P2 matrix match the actual code in src/services/interfaces and the implemented pages.
findings: Wrote /projects/sandbox/PSA/README.md documenting the zero-dependency Node.js 22 built-ins stack, the required `unset NODE_OPTIONS` caveat, exact build/seed/test/start commands (matched to package.json scripts and default port 4000), directory layout, the 16-table schema (15 core entities + rips), all six interface seams (Recognizer, PricingEngine, ClassificationService, ListingGenerator, MarketplacePublisher, SellerAssistant) with real drop-in guidance, a P0/P1/P2 status matrix, demo data (is_demo, demo@pokeops.local / pokeops-demo from seed.ts), security notes (scrypt+salt, cookie sessions, no marketplace creds in frontend), and known limitations (in-memory session store, experimental node:sqlite). Verified: `unset NODE_OPTIONS; npm run build && npm run seed && npm test` all succeed; 119/119 tests pass. Every README claim was checked against actual code (schema.ts, interfaces/*, mock/*, seed.ts, config, session.ts). Note: schema defines 16 tables total (15 core + rips added in FEAT-007); README states this explicitly. Committed on main.
